learning_outcomes.text: Students can have basic grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation knowledge at an introductory level (A1).

(Reading) Students can gain basic reading comprehension skills, read simple texts, grasp the main ideas of texts, examine the concept and structure of paragraphs and understand their function in the text, and recognize basic English text types.

(Writing) Students can write short compositions on a specific topic, express their opinions in writing related to the unit's topic, summarize short texts (such as newspaper articles), and be aware of spelling and punctuation rules.

(Listening) Students can have listening comprehension skills, recognize grammatical patterns in speech, distinguish different discourse types (daily conversation, formal speech, interview, talk-show, private conversations, etc.), and fill in blanks by following the book's instructions (listening for main ideas, listening for details, etc.).

(Speaking) Students can answer short questions on familiar topics such as "Introducing oneself, family information, favorite things," create short dialogues, express their ideas related to the unit's discussion topics, and use vocabulary appropriate to their level (e.g., expressing basic needs, asking about instructions or directions).
Students can communicate at a minimum level with learned material.
